## Choice of cosine estimator (note re: issue body)

The issue body's `cos(π · (1 − 2h/(k·d)))` form gives −1 at h=0 (perfect match), which inverts the convention. Implementation uses the canonical Charikar `cos(π · h / (k·d))`, matching what `tests/test_core.py` already uses for the 1-bit case. The variance-reduction claim is independent of the exact analytical estimator, so the test asserts on raw `h / (k·d)` rather than the cosine-mapped form.

q.fit(X_train)              # no-op, sklearn-style ergonomics

# Implement 1-bit SignBitQuantizer (closes #2)

Core SimHash quantizer for v0.1.0 — Haar-distributed rotation, sign-packed codes, popcount-LUT Hamming search. Class API plus the functional primitives the spec requires (`haar_rotation`, `encode_signs`, `hamming_search`) re-exported from `remax.core`.

## What's in
- `src/remax/rotation.py` — `haar_rotation(d, seed)`
- `src/remax/packing.py` — `encode_signs`, `hamming_distances`, `hamming_search`, `POPCOUNT_LUT`
- `src/remax/core.py` — `SignBitQuantizer` + functional re-exports
- `src/remax/__init__.py` — public surface; `__version__ = "0.0.0"` (release bump deferred to #6)
- `tests/test_core.py` — 23 tests, all 5 spec requirements covered, green in ~1.9s
- `bench/smoke_1bit.py` — R@10 = 0.720 at default; 0.679 at `--n 5000 --queries 200 --seed 42`

## Three deliberate deviations from the issue text

Each is commented in-line where it lands, but flagging up-front:

### 1. `haar_rotation` includes Mezzadri sign correction
The issue shows `np.linalg.qr(...)[0]`. That's uniform on a fundamental domain of O(d), not on O(d) itself — and the function name promises Haar measure. One extra line, preserves orthogonality, no test cost. Single-machine determinism only; cross-BLAS Householder is post-v0.1.0 (remex's pattern noted in the docstring for when it matters).

### 2. The Spearman test plants known cosines
At d=768, pure isotropic Gaussian pairwise cosines concentrate around 0 with stdev ≈ 1/√d ≈ 0.036 — the same order as the SimHash noise floor at 768 bits. SNR ≈ 1, so ρ caps near 0.6 by construction regardless of encoder quality. The test as literally written in the spec is mathematically unachievable on the input distribution it specifies.

Fix: construct vectors with explicit target cosines `X[i] = w[i]·anchor + √(1-w[i]²)·v_perp[i]` with `w ~ U(-1, 1)` and `v_perp` orthogonalized Gaussian directions, so `cos(X[i], anchor) == w[i]` exactly. Restores the dynamic range the test implicitly assumes. ρ > 0.95 passes cleanly. Rationale documented in the test docstring.

### 3. Smoke bench uses low-rank Gaussian, not isotropic
Same concentration-of-measure problem at a different metric:
- Isotropic Gaussian: R@10 ≈ 0.21 (chance-level)
- Gaussian mixture, unit-norm centers + scaled noise: R@10 ≈ 0.30. Cluster identification works; within-cluster cosines pack into a ≈0.015-wide band that's below 768-bit rank resolution.
- Low-rank Gaussian (data drawn from a `subdim`-dim Gaussian embedded in d via random orthonormal basis): clean continuous spread.

Empirical sweep at d=768, n=1000:

| `--subdim` | R@10 |
|---|---|
| 8 | 0.854 |
| 16 | 0.801 |
| 32 | 0.720 (default) |
| 64 | 0.632 |
| 128 | 0.521 |

All clear the > 0.5 bar. Real text embeddings concentrate on a low-dim manifold for the same reason, so this is also closer to the operating regime the library is designed for. Bench docstring documents all three options and why the picked one is right.

## Other notes
- 256-entry uint16 popcount LUT, not `np.unpackbits` — same idiom remex uses, ~8× less memory churn. SIMD kernels are post-v0.1.0.
- Rotation initialized eagerly in `__init__`; `fit()` is a sklearn-compat no-op that optionally validates `X` shape. Matches the spec's "X_train optional, only for shape" language.
- Per-query loop in batched search; vectorized would need an (m, n, B) intermediate (~GB at typical sizes). Justifying full vectorization needs SIMD popcount.
- Bench cost: encode 1000×768 → (1000, 96) in ~95 ms; search 100 queries in ~33 ms (0.33 ms/q).

## Test coverage
All 5 spec requirements:
1. ✅ Rotation orthogonality `R @ R.T ≈ I` to 1e-6 (parametric over d=8/64/128/768)
2. ✅ Determinism — byte-identical codes for same seed
3. ✅ Spearman ρ > 0.95 (with planted-cosine construction; see §2 above)
4. ✅ Self-recall@1 ≥ 95% on isotropic Gaussian
5. ✅ `d % 8 != 0` raises clear error

Plus: parametric orthogonality, functional/class parity, search shape, batched search, hamming symmetry, fit validation, k>n clamping, encode accepting single vector, codes shape validation.
